case.name: Ikpoki
case.summary: IKPOKI: five wells, four markers the course never uses (TOP_M, TOP_RES, BASE_RES, TOP_L); TOP_M faulted out of Ikpoki-5, Ikpoki-3 stopped above TOP_L. Beginner hangs it on TOP_RES at 2100 m, intermediate on TOP_M at 2050 m (Ikpoki-5 flagged), advanced predicts Ikpoki-3 TOP_L two ways.

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section TOP_RES is picked at 2161, 2143, 2187, 2170 and 2133 m in Ikpoki-1 to Ikpoki-5. What is the structural relief of TOP_RES, and which wells set it?
beginner.correct: {{relief_TOP_RES}} m over all five wells, from Ikpoki-5 at 2133 m down to Ikpoki-3 at 2187 m, the two extremes.
distractors: {{relief_TOP_RES_4}} m, from Ikpoki-2 at 2143 m down to Ikpoki-3 at 2187 m, leaving out Ikpoki-5 because it lacks TOP_M.
{{res_thick_spread}} m, the gap between the thickest and the thinnest reservoir in the five wells.
None, because a panel flattened on TOP_RES draws the surface as one level line in every well.
beginner.explanation: Relief is the deepest pick less the shallowest over every well that carries the surface: 2187 less 2133 is {{relief_TOP_RES}} m, and Ikpoki-5 carries TOP_RES even though it lacks TOP_M.
why_wrong: drops a well that carries the surface because it lacks a different top
quotes a thickness spread where one surface's relief was asked
reads relief off the view that removed it

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section TOP_L is picked at 2257, 2245, 2263 and 2227 m in Ikpoki-1, -2, -4 and -5. Ikpoki-3 reached total depth above TOP_L, and it is the deepest well on every surface it does reach. How should TOP_L relief be reported?
beginner.correct: As {{relief_TOP_L}} m over four wells, probably understated because the deepest well, Ikpoki-3, is the one missing.
distractors: As {{wrong_reliefL_zero}} m over five wells, reading the missing Ikpoki-3 pick as zero so every well is counted.
As {{relief_TOP_L}} m over five wells, since a missing top is still part of the section.
As {{L_disp_B_spread}} m over four wells, read off the TOP_L line on a panel flattened on TOP_RES at 2100 m.
beginner.explanation: 2263 less 2227 is {{relief_TOP_L}} m over the four wells that carry TOP_L. Ikpoki-3 would most likely have supplied the deepest pick, so the figure is biased low and the well count must travel with it.
why_wrong: treats a missing top as a depth of zero
quotes a four-well number as if it covered five wells
reads a structural quantity off a flattened view

beginner.prompt: Flatten the Ikpoki section on TOP_RES at a 2100 m datum. TOP_RES is picked at 2161, 2143, 2187, 2170 and 2133 m in Ikpoki-1 to Ikpoki-5. What is Ikpoki-3's shift, and which way does its column move?
beginner.correct: {{shiftB_I3}} m, and the column moves up the display, since its pick lies deeper than the datum.
distractors: +{{wrong_shiftB_I3}} m, taking the pick less the datum, so the column slides down the display toward deeper values.
{{shiftB_I3}} m, and the column moves down the display, because a negative shift adds depth to every pick.
Minus {{relief_TOP_RES}} m, the distance from the shallowest TOP_RES pick on the section down to this well's pick.
beginner.explanation: The shift is the datum less the pick: 2100 less 2187 is {{shiftB_I3}} m. Adding a negative number gives a shallower displayed depth, so the well rises, and it rises furthest of the five because its pick is deepest.
why_wrong: reverses the subtraction
gets the number right and the direction wrong
measures from another well's pick instead of the datum

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_RES at 2100 m, Ikpoki-3 takes a shift of {{shiftB_I3}} m. Its BASE_RES is picked at 2212 m. Where does BASE_RES display?
beginner.correct: At {{I3_base_disp_B}} m, a position on the picture with nothing in Ikpoki-3 at that measured depth.
distractors: At {{wrong_I3_base_disp_B}} m, adding {{wrong_shiftB_I3}} m because the column is pushed down to meet the datum.
At {{wrong_I3_base_disp_B_w1}} m, using the {{shiftB_I1}} m shift of Ikpoki-1, the first well on the section.
At 2212 m, since only the datum top is moved and every other pick keeps its measured depth.
beginner.explanation: Every depth in a well takes that well's one shift: 2212 plus {{shiftB_I3}} is {{I3_base_disp_B}} m. It is a displayed depth, a place on the panel, and no rock in Ikpoki-3 sits at that measured depth.
why_wrong: flips the sign of the shift
applies another well's shift
moves only the datum top

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_RES at 2100 m, Ikpoki-3's reservoir zone displays from {{I3_res_top_disp_B}} m to {{I3_res_base_disp_B}} m. What is its gross thickness, and what does that figure include?
beginner.correct: {{res_thick_I3}} m on any view, counting every metre between TOP_RES and BASE_RES, shale included.
distractors: {{res_thick_I3}} m of net pay, since the flattened view strips the shale beds out of the zone before it draws the fill.
{{I3_res_base_disp_B}} m, the displayed depth of the zone base, which is the thickness hanging below the datum line.
{{wrong_crosswell_thick}} m, BASE_RES in Ikpoki-3 less TOP_RES in Ikpoki-2.
beginner.explanation: Both ends of the zone carry the same shift, so it cancels: {{I3_res_base_disp_B}} less {{I3_res_top_disp_B}} is {{res_thick_I3}} m, the same as 2212 less 2187. Correlation gives gross thickness only; net pay needs log cutoffs.
why_wrong: calls a gross thickness net pay
quotes a displayed depth as a thickness
subtracts picks from two different wells

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section the reservoir is {{res_thick_I1}}, {{res_thick_I2}}, {{res_thick_I3}}, {{res_thick_I4}} and {{res_thick_I5}} m thick in Ikpoki-1 to Ikpoki-5, while TOP_RES moves {{relief_TOP_RES}} m across the same wells. Why is the thickness pattern hard to see on the structural section?
beginner.correct: Its {{res_thick_spread}} m spread of thickness is small beside the {{relief_TOP_RES}} m the surface itself moves, so it draws as a sliver.
distractors: The structural view shifts each well by its own amount before drawing, which scrambles the zone thicknesses.
Thickness grows with depth here, so the deepest well always looks the thickest on any panel.
A structural section cannot draw thickness at all, since it shows only one top in each well column.
beginner.explanation: Thickness varies by {{res_thick_spread}} m, from {{res_thick_I3}} m in Ikpoki-3 to {{res_thick_I2}} m in Ikpoki-2, while the structure moves {{relief_TOP_RES}} m, so the signal you want is a small fraction of the panel. The deepest well, Ikpoki-3, is in fact the thinnest.
why_wrong: describes flattening, which the structural view does not do
contradicted by the deepest well being the thinnest
a structural section draws every top in every well

beginner.prompt: The Ikpoki tops table has TOP_M in four wells (it is faulted out of Ikpoki-5), TOP_RES and BASE_RES in all five, and TOP_L in four (Ikpoki-3 stopped above it). Which surfaces make a clean flattening datum for the whole section?
beginner.correct: TOP_RES and BASE_RES, the only two surfaces every one of the five wells carries.
distractors: TOP_M, because it is the shallowest marker and the rest hangs below it.
TOP_L, since the deepest surface sits below every zone of interest and isolates everything above it.
Any of the four, since the engine fills a missing datum pick from the average of the neighbouring wells.
beginner.explanation: A datum top must be present in every well to flatten the whole section. TOP_M leaves Ikpoki-5 unflattened and TOP_L leaves Ikpoki-3 unflattened, while TOP_RES and BASE_RES are carried by all {{carriers_TOP_RES}} wells.
why_wrong: Ikpoki-5 has no TOP_M, so it would hang unflattened
Ikpoki-3 has no TOP_L, so it would hang unflattened
the engine never guesses a datum pick

beginner.prompt: You flatten the Ikpoki section on TOP_M at a 2100 m datum. TOP_M is faulted out of Ikpoki-5, whose TOP_RES is picked at 2133 m. Where does Ikpoki-5's TOP_RES display?
beginner.correct: At {{I5_res_disp_onM}} m, its measured depth: the well takes no shift and is flagged.
distractors: At 2100 m, since the engine hangs every well's reservoir on the datum line when one top is missing.
At {{wrong_I5_res_meanshift}} m, using the mean shift of the four wells that do carry TOP_M.
Nowhere, since a well lacking the datum top is dropped from the flattened panel.
beginner.explanation: A well without the datum top has nothing to subtract from the datum, so the engine gives it a null shift and draws every pick at measured depth, here {{I5_res_disp_onM}} m, and flags it. It never borrows a shift from the neighbours.
why_wrong: the engine never re-hangs a well on another top
the engine never borrows a shift from other wells
the well stays on the panel, flagged

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_RES at 2100 m, Ikpoki-2's TOP_L (picked at 2245 m) displays at {{L_disp_B_I2}} m. Its TOP_RES pick of 2143 m turns out to be 9 m too shallow; the true pick is {{mispick_I2_res}} m. What changes?
beginner.correct: TOP_L now displays at {{mispick_L_disp_I2}} m, while its measured BASE_RES to TOP_L interval stays {{true_res_L_I2}} m.
distractors: TOP_L stays at {{L_disp_B_I2}} m, since only the corrected pick itself moves on the flattened panel.
The whole panel slides 9 m for every well, so nothing is compared any differently than before.
The TOP_RES picks stop lining up at 2100 m, and that misalignment is how the panel reveals the error.
beginner.explanation: The shift becomes 2100 less {{mispick_I2_res}}, which is {{mispick_shift_I2}} m, so every pick in Ikpoki-2 moves with it and TOP_L displays at {{mispick_L_disp_I2}} m. The datum picks always line up, so the flattened view cannot show a datum pick error.
why_wrong: a datum pick moves every surface in its well
only one well's shift changes
the datum surface is level by construction whatever the picks

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section TOP_M is faulted out of Ikpoki-5 and Ikpoki-3 stopped drilling above TOP_L. How many wells do the TOP_M and TOP_L correlation lines each reach, and why?
beginner.correct: Four each: the TOP_M line skips Ikpoki-5 and the TOP_L line skips Ikpoki-3, and neither gap is filled.
distractors: Five each, since the engine carries every line across the whole section and fills each gap.
Three each, since a line is drawn only between wells that carry all four of the tops.
Four and five, since a faulted-out top is drawn at the fault depth in that well.
beginner.explanation: The engine walks the wells and skips any well without the top, adding no point: TOP_M reaches {{line_TOP_M}} wells and TOP_L reaches {{line_TOP_L}}. A line that stops short is information.
why_wrong: the engine never interpolates across a gap
a line needs only its own top in each well
nothing is drawn where there is no pick

beginner.prompt: The Ikpoki tops table shows TOP_M missing in Ikpoki-5 and TOP_L missing in Ikpoki-3, whose deepest pick is BASE_RES at 2212 m. Ikpoki-5 carries TOP_RES, BASE_RES and TOP_L. Which gap can the section itself explain?
beginner.correct: The Ikpoki-3 gap: its picks end above where TOP_L would lie, so the well stopped short.
distractors: The Ikpoki-5 gap, since a shallow marker missing above deeper markers that are present proves erosion.
Both, since any gap in a tops table means the well reached total depth above that surface.
Neither, because a gap only ever means the interpreter has not got round to picking it yet.
beginner.explanation: Only total depth above the surface is knowable from the section, and Ikpoki-3's deepest pick is BASE_RES. A shallow gap in Ikpoki-5 could be faulting, erosion or an unpicked top, and each needs evidence from outside the section.
why_wrong: absence alone is never proof of erosion
Ikpoki-5 reaches deeper than TOP_M, so total depth cannot explain it
one of the four reasons is readable here

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_RES at 2100 m, the engine reports a displayed range of {{rangeB_min}} m to {{rangeB_max}} m. Which picks set its two ends?
beginner.correct: Ikpoki-3's TOP_M at the top and Ikpoki-2's TOP_L at the base.
distractors: Ikpoki-2's TOP_M at the top and Ikpoki-4's TOP_L at the base, the shallowest and deepest measured picks.
Ikpoki-5's TOP_RES at the top and Ikpoki-3's BASE_RES at the base, the two ends of the reservoir.
The datum line at the top and Ikpoki-4's TOP_L at the base.
beginner.explanation: Displayed depth is the datum plus the distance from each well's own TOP_RES. Ikpoki-3 has the longest TOP_M to TOP_RES gap, so its TOP_M displays highest at {{I3_M_disp_B}} m, and Ikpoki-2's TOP_L sits furthest below its TOP_RES, displaying at {{L_disp_B_I2}} m.
why_wrong: measured extremes are not displayed extremes
reservoir picks sit near the datum
TOP_M displays above the datum

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_RES at 2100 m, the TOP_L line displays at {{L_disp_B_I1}}, {{L_disp_B_I2}}, {{L_disp_B_I4}} and {{L_disp_B_I5}} m. A colleague reports TOP_L relief as {{L_disp_B_spread}} m. What is wrong?
beginner.correct: Relief is structural and must come from the measured picks: {{relief_TOP_L}} m over the four wells with TOP_L.
distractors: Nothing, since flattening keeps every depth difference between wells as well as within them.
The spread must include Ikpoki-3 at the datum depth, which widens it to cover all five wells.
The figure should be doubled, since flattening halves the apparent relief of each deeper surface.
beginner.explanation: Differences between wells change under flattening because each well has its own shift. The {{L_disp_B_spread}} m spread describes TOP_L relative to TOP_RES; relief is 2263 less 2227, {{relief_TOP_L}} m over four wells.
why_wrong: only within-well differences survive flattening
Ikpoki-3 has no TOP_L to include
no such halving rule exists

beginner.prompt: On the Ikpoki section TOP_RES is picked at 2161, 2143, 2187, 2170 and 2133 m in Ikpoki-1 to Ikpoki-5. Where must a TOP_RES datum sit for every shift to be positive?
beginner.correct: Deeper than 2187 m, the deepest TOP_RES pick, so every column moves down the display.
distractors: Shallower than 2133 m, the shallowest pick, since a positive shift lifts each column up toward the datum.
Anywhere at all, since the sign of a shift follows the structure of each well and not the datum.
Exactly at 2187 m, so that one well takes a zero shift and the rest turn positive.
beginner.explanation: The shift is the datum less the pick, so it is positive only where the datum is deeper than the pick; for all five that means deeper than Ikpoki-3's 2187 m. At exactly 2187 m Ikpoki-3's shift is zero, which is not positive.
why_wrong: a shallow datum gives negative shifts
the sign is set by the datum
zero is not positive

intermediate.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_M at a 2050 m datum: TOP_M is picked at 2104, 2090, 2121 and 2112 m in Ikpoki-1 to Ikpoki-4 and is faulted out of Ikpoki-5. What is Ikpoki-3's shift, and how does it compare with the other hung wells?
intermediate.correct: {{shiftI_I3}} m, the largest move up the display of the four hung wells.
distractors: 71 m downward, taking the pick less the datum, the largest move of the four hung wells.
{{shiftI_I4}} m, since Ikpoki-4 carries the deepest TOP_M and so Ikpoki-3 moves less.
{{shiftB_I3}} m, the shift it takes when the section is hung on TOP_RES at 2100 m.
intermediate.explanation: 2050 less 2121 is {{shiftI_I3}} m. Ikpoki-3 has the deepest TOP_M, so it travels furthest up to reach the datum; the others take {{shiftI_I1}}, {{shiftI_I2}} and {{shiftI_I4}} m.
why_wrong: reverses the subtraction
Ikpoki-4's TOP_M at 2112 m is shallower than Ikpoki-3's
uses a different flattening top and datum

intermediate.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_M at a 2050 m datum, Ikpoki-2 takes a shift of {{shiftI_I2}} m. Its TOP_RES is picked at 2143 m. Where does TOP_RES display, and what does that number measure?
intermediate.correct: At {{RES_disp_I_I2}} m, the datum plus Ikpoki-2's own TOP_M to TOP_RES interval of {{MtoRES_I2}} m.
distractors: At 2143 m, its measured depth, since only the flattening top moves and the rest stays in place.
At {{wrong_RES_disp_I_I2}} m, subtracting the shift, which is what moves a deep pick up the display.
At 2050 m, since every correlated surface lines up at the datum once a section is flattened.
intermediate.explanation: 2143 plus {{shiftI_I2}} is {{RES_disp_I_I2}} m, which is 2050 plus the {{MtoRES_I2}} m between Ikpoki-2's TOP_M and TOP_RES. On this datum a displayed depth is the datum plus the distance below the well's own TOP_M.
why_wrong: every pick in the well takes the shift
adding a negative shift already moves the pick up
only the flattening top lines up

intermediate.prompt: Flatten the Ikpoki section on TOP_RES at a 2160 m datum instead. TOP_RES is picked at 2161, 2143, 2187, 2170 and 2133 m in Ikpoki-1 to Ikpoki-5. How do the shifts come out?
intermediate.correct: {{mix_positive}} positive and {{mix_negative}} negative: Ikpoki-2 and Ikpoki-5 move down and the other three move up.
distractors: All five negative, since a flattening shift is always the datum less a deeper pick.
Mixed, which shows the TOP_RES picks in Ikpoki-2 and Ikpoki-5 are wrong and need re-picking.
{{mix_negative}} positive and {{mix_positive}} negative, since wells deeper than the datum move down to meet it.
intermediate.explanation: A datum inside the range of picks gives mixed signs: Ikpoki-2 takes +{{shiftMix_I2}} m and Ikpoki-5 +{{shiftMix_I5}} m, the others {{shiftMix_I1}}, {{shiftMix_I3}} and {{shiftMix_I4}} m. Nothing is broken; the wells converge on the datum from both sides.
why_wrong: two picks are shallower than 2160 m
a mixed sign is a property of the datum
wells deeper than the datum move up

intermediate.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_M at a 2050 m datum, the TOP_M to TOP_RES intervals of the four hung wells are {{MtoRES_I1}}, {{MtoRES_I2}}, {{MtoRES_I3}} and {{MtoRES_I4}} m. What is the growth range, and over how many wells?
intermediate.correct: {{growth_MtoRES}} m over four wells, from Ikpoki-2 at {{MtoRES_I2}} m to Ikpoki-3 at {{MtoRES_I3}} m.
distractors: {{relief_TOP_RES}} m over five wells, the spread of TOP_RES from Ikpoki-5 to Ikpoki-3.
{{relief_TOP_RES_4}} m over four wells, the spread of measured TOP_RES in the wells with TOP_M.
{{res_thick_spread}} m over five wells, the spread of the TOP_RES to BASE_RES thickness.
intermediate.explanation: Growth range is the largest interval less the smallest: {{MtoRES_I3}} less {{MtoRES_I2}} is {{growth_MtoRES}} m, over the four wells that carry both TOP_M and TOP_RES. Relief figures describe one surface, and this question names an interval.
why_wrong: relief of one surface, asked for an interval
relief of the lower surface mixes structure and growth
a different interval

intermediate.prompt: Over the four Ikpoki wells that carry TOP_M, TOP_M relief is {{relief_TOP_M}} m, TOP_RES relief is {{relief_TOP_RES_4}} m and the TOP_M to TOP_RES growth range is {{growth_MtoRES}} m. Why is the TOP_RES relief exactly the sum of the other two here?
intermediate.correct: Ikpoki-3 has the deepest TOP_M and the thickest interval, and Ikpoki-2 the shallowest and the thinnest.
distractors: The sum is a law of flattening that holds on every section, whichever wells hold the extremes.
Relief and growth are the same quantity read on two views, and the sum just rounds them together.
The match is a coincidence of these picks and says nothing about structure or interval thickness.
intermediate.explanation: TOP_RES depth is TOP_M depth plus the interval in each well, so its spread is at most {{relief_TOP_M}} plus {{growth_MtoRES}} m, and equals it only when one well holds both deep extremes and another both shallow ones, as Ikpoki-3 and Ikpoki-2 do.
why_wrong: in general the sum is only an upper bound
relief is structural, growth stratigraphic
the equality has a stated cause

intermediate.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_M at a 2050 m datum, the engine reports a displayed range of {{rangeI_min}} m to {{rangeI_max}} m. Where does the deep end come from?
intermediate.correct: Ikpoki-5's TOP_L at its measured {{rangeI_max}} m, because a well lacking TOP_M hangs unshifted.
distractors: Ikpoki-4's TOP_L, the deepest measured pick on the whole section, hung on the datum like the rest.
Ikpoki-2's TOP_L, which sits the greatest distance below its own TOP_M of any well.
Ikpoki-3's BASE_RES, since the well with the deepest TOP_M always owns the deep end.
intermediate.explanation: The engine draws a well without the datum top at measured depth and still counts it in the range, so Ikpoki-5's TOP_L at {{rangeI_max}} m sets the base and the span reads {{spanI}} m.
why_wrong: Ikpoki-4 is hung and displays shallower
true for the hung wells, but Ikpoki-5 is drawn deeper
Ikpoki-3 stops far short below its TOP_M

intermediate.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_M at a 2050 m datum, set Ikpoki-5 aside. Over the four hung wells, what is the displayed span, and which well owns its deep end?
intermediate.correct: {{spanI4}} m, owned by Ikpoki-2, whose TOP_L lies {{below_M_I2}} m below its own TOP_M.
distractors: {{spanI}} m, owned by Ikpoki-5's TOP_L, which the engine draws at its measured depth.
{{below_M_I4}} m, owned by Ikpoki-4, which carries the deepest TOP_L on the section.
{{below_M_I3}} m, owned by Ikpoki-3, which carries the deepest TOP_M on the section.
intermediate.explanation: On a TOP_M datum the shallow end is pinned at 2050 m, so the span equals the largest distance below TOP_M: {{below_M_I1}}, {{below_M_I2}}, {{below_M_I3}} and {{below_M_I4}} m, largest in Ikpoki-2.
why_wrong: includes the unhung well
deepest measured pick is not deepest displayed
Ikpoki-3 stopped short of TOP_L

intermediate.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_M at a 2050 m datum, you move the datum to {{datum_I_deeper}} m and keep TOP_M as the flattening top. What changes?
intermediate.correct: Every shift moves by {{datum_move}} m, Ikpoki-3's to {{shiftI2_I3}} m, and the {{spanI4}} m span of the hung wells holds.
distractors: The span grows by {{datum_move}} m, since every displayed depth moves {{datum_move}} m deeper on the panel.
The growth range grows by {{datum_move}} m, because the intervals are read below the datum line.
Nothing at all, since the shifts are fixed by the picks and do not depend on the datum depth.
intermediate.explanation: Moving the datum slides the whole picture: each shift changes by {{datum_move}} m, so Ikpoki-3's becomes 2080 less 2121, {{shiftI2_I3}} m. Spans and intervals are differences, so they do not move.
why_wrong: both ends move together
intervals do not depend on the datum
the shift is the datum less the pick

intermediate.prompt: On the Ikpoki section TOP_M is faulted out of Ikpoki-5 and TOP_L was never reached in Ikpoki-3; the other three wells carry all four tops. How many wells carry all four tops?
intermediate.correct: {{wells_all_four}} of the five wells: Ikpoki-3 lacks TOP_L and Ikpoki-5 lacks TOP_M.
distractors: {{picks_present}} of {{pick_slots}}, the count of picks present across the five wells and four tops.
Four, because a well missing only its shallowest marker still has a complete reservoir.
{{wells_missing_one}}, the number of wells that each lack one of the four tops.
intermediate.explanation: The count is of wells, and a well counts only with every one of the four tops. Two wells each miss one, so {{wells_all_four}} remain. The {{picks_present}} of {{pick_slots}} pick count is a different measure.
why_wrong: counts picks instead of wells
every one of the four tops is required
counts the wells that fail

intermediate.prompt: You want the Ikpoki TOP_M to TOP_RES growth on one flattened panel. TOP_M is faulted out of Ikpoki-5. Which flattening top serves that question best, and what does it cost?
intermediate.correct: TOP_M, accepting that Ikpoki-5 hangs unshifted and flagged and that TOP_M relief leaves the view.
distractors: TOP_RES, since all five wells carry it, so the growth reads down from it in every well.
TOP_L, since the deepest surface isolates everything above it and costs nothing.
BASE_RES, since flattening below an interval shows its growth without spending a surface.
intermediate.explanation: Flattening on the top of the interval makes each displayed TOP_RES the datum plus that well's interval, so growth reads directly. Ikpoki-5 has no TOP_M and so no such interval on any view, so the question never covered it; the cost is a flagged column and the {{relief_TOP_M}} m of TOP_M relief.
why_wrong: on TOP_RES the interval reads upward, not from one line
Ikpoki-3 lacks TOP_L
every flattening spends one surface

intermediate.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_M at a 2050 m datum, Ikpoki-5 is drawn unshifted with TOP_RES at 2133 m and TOP_L at 2227 m. Can its TOP_RES to TOP_L interval be read off this panel?
intermediate.correct: Yes, {{RtoL_I5}} m, since both picks sit in one column and an interval needs no shift.
distractors: No, because a flagged well's picks mean nothing until the well is hung on the datum.
Yes, but it reads {{spanI_excess}} m too long because that well was never flattened.
No, since the engine drops the zone fill for any well that lacks the datum top.
intermediate.explanation: An interval is two picks in one well, and a shift, null or not, applies to both, so 2227 less 2133 is {{RtoL_I5}} m on any view. What the flagged well cannot give is a comparison of displayed depths against the hung wells.
why_wrong: within-well intervals are view-independent
the extra span is a between-well effect
zone spans need only their two tops

intermediate.prompt: On the Ikpoki section flattened on TOP_M at a 2050 m datum, the displayed TOP_RES picks are {{RES_disp_I_I1}}, {{RES_disp_I_I2}}, {{RES_disp_I_I3}}, {{RES_disp_I_I4}} and {{RES_disp_I_I5}} m. A colleague quotes the growth range as {{wrong_growth_with_I5}} m. What is it?
intermediate.correct: {{growth_MtoRES}} m from the four hung wells, since Ikpoki-5's {{RES_disp_I_I5}} m is a measured depth.
distractors: {{wrong_growth_with_I5}} m, the full spread of the displayed TOP_RES line across all five wells.
{{relief_TOP_RES}} m, since a growth range must always be read from the measured depths.
{{growth_MtoBASE}} m, the spread of the TOP_M to BASE_RES interval in the hung wells.
intermediate.explanation: The fast reading works only in wells hung on TOP_M: {{RES_disp_I_I3}} less {{RES_disp_I_I2}} is {{growth_MtoRES}} m, matching the intervals. Ikpoki-5 has no TOP_M, so it has no TOP_M to TOP_RES interval at all.
why_wrong: mixes an unhung well into a displayed spread
that is relief of one surface
